items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: So Beasley had a 9-piece orchestra to take to Poughkeepsie. We worked 4 days a week...

ctx.x: But Metcalf could play and he had a fine style with plenty of technique. He never wore his crown after Louis Armstrong left. It was one of the greatest thrills of my life to have heard this man who was destined to do so much for jazz.

One week before the end of June, Dickie Wells came to my house and said that he had a job for us with a drummer he knew by the name of Dewey Beasley. We met Beasley and he told us that the job was up-state in a place called Poughkeepsie, New York. This was Dewey's home town and the job was at a place called Woodcliff Park, which was an amusement park. The job didn't pay much but we could live and have a little group of our own.

So Dickie, myself, Mack Walker, Harold McFerran, and Don Frye got together again with 'Bull' Williams, an alto player from Dayton, Ohio named Melvin Scott and a tenor named Bobby Sands. So Beasley had a 9-piece orchestra to take to Poughkeepsie. We worked 4 days a week, Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays and played matinees on special occasions and holidays which were not many in the summer.
